summary: Conditional aggregation counts or adds only some rows within each group, by putting CASE inside an aggregate.
points: SUM(CASE WHEN condition THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) counts matching rows.
SUM(CASE WHEN condition THEN amount ELSE 0 END) adds matching amounts.
Dividing by COUNT(*) gives a percentage. Multiply by 100.0 to keep decimals.
Unlike WHERE, this keeps every group, even one with no matches.

example.sql:
SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS orders,
  ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'shipped' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 1) AS shipped_pct
FROM orders
GROUP BY customer_id;
example.explanation: Each customer gets a total order count and a percentage shipped.
